Pt(553) single-crystal preparation (Clavilier method)
nodes.procedure: Bead-type Pt(553) electrodes were prepared following the Clavilier method before every experiment; the electrode was flame annealed for 1 min, allowed to cool in an Ar/H2 (3:1) atmosphere and then dipped into ultrapure water saturated with the same gas mixture. Transfer through air to the electrochemical cell occurred while the surface of the electrode was protected with a droplet of water.
nodes.source_text: Bead-type Pt(111) and Pt(553) electrodes were prepared following the Clavilier method37 before every experiment; the electrode was flame annealed for 1 min, allowed to cool in an Ar/H2 (3:1) atmosphere...

nodes.name: Selective step-edge decoration with metal adatoms
nodes.procedure: Metal adatoms (Mo, Re, Ru, Rh, Ag) were deposited selectively at the Pt(553) step edge by transferring the flame-annealed electrode to 0.1 M HClO4 electrolyte containing 10^{-4} to 10^{-7} M metal precursor ions (sodium molybdate for Mo, ammonium perrhenate for Re, RuCl3 for Ru, rhodium chloride for Rh, silver perchlorate for Ag) and cycling between 0.05-0.35 V_RHE for 10-200 cycles. Concentration and cycle number controlled coverage. For Mo/Re-decorated electrodes, transfer to alkaline electrolyte for HER testing was done under H2 atmosphere to prevent desorption.

nodes.characterization_summary: CVs confirm selective step decoration: bare Pt(553) shows H adsorption on terrace (0.06-0.3 V_RHE), sharp step edge H/OH/H2O exchange peak (0.125 V_RHE), and terrace OH adsorption (0.6-0.85 V_RHE). Ru* decoration eliminates step edge peak at 0.125 V_RHE while terrace H adsorption unaffected, confirming step-selective Ru* deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CV in 0.1 M HClO4 in Fig. 1b shows three features: a broad peak due to hydrogen adsorption on (111)-like terrace sites (0.06-0.3 V_RHE), a sharp peak due to an exchange between hydrogen and co-adsorbed hydroxide and water at the (110) step edge (0.125 V_RHE) (ref. 25) and a peak at high potentials due to the adsorption of hydroxide on the (111)-like terrace (0.6-0.85 V_RHE). The voltammogram measured after the deposition of Ru shows that the Ru* blocks the adsorption of the hydrogen and hydroxide at the Pt step edge, which eliminates the sharp peak at 0.125 V_RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT confirms Re*, Ru*, Rh* at Pt(553) step have small/negligible effect on terrace H* binding strength (Supplementary Fig. 2). Ag* at step affects terrace H binding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations support that the presence of Re, Ru and Rh at the step have only a small or negligible effect on the binding strength of hydrogen to the terrace (Supplementary Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS measured H UPD kinetics on step-decorated Pt(553) (10^4-0.5 Hz, 5 mV amplitude) using equivalent circuit fitted to impedance spectra.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The kinetics of the hydrogen underpotential deposition were measured using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Impedance spectra were measured with frequencies from 10^4 to 0.5 Hz with an amplitude of 5 mV. An equivalent circuit was fitted to the impedance spectra using the EIS Spectrum Analyser.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT-calculated OH* adsorption free energies at 0 V_RHE show volcano relationship with experimental HER activity for Pt(553) decorated with Mo*, Re*, Ru*, Rh*, Ag* at step edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 illustrates that the experimentally measured rate of the HER in an alkaline electrolyte follows a volcano type relationship with the DFT-calculated binding strength of hydroxide on the adatom at the step.
